prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “AI recommendation checker.” Instead use a mix of local-SEO/listing management services, entity/knowledge-graph APIs, reputation tools, and direct testing of LLMs. That combination lets you both maximize the chance an AI will surface your business and verify whether different AI engines actually mention or recommend you.

What to use (best options, by purpose)
- Ensure presence and accuracy (most important, free first step)
  - Google Business Profile (free) — essential for Google/Maps and many AI results that draw on Google’s Knowledge Graph.
  - Apple Maps Connect, Bing Places, Yelp, Facebook Business — other major directories.

- Manage citations/listings at scale (best paid services)
  - Yext or BrightLocal — sync and fix listings across directories (good ROI for local visibility).
  - Moz Local, Whitespark — alternatives focused on local citations and local SEO.

- Reputation/review monitoring (influences AI recommendations)
  - Podium, Reputation.com, Chatmeter — monitor and collect reviews across platforms.

- Knowledge-graph / entity presence (how AIs discover businesses)
  - Google Knowledge Graph / Google Places API — check if your business appears as an entity.
  - Bing Entity Search API — similar for Microsoft/Bing-backed models.

- Search & SERP tracking (indirectly shows what AIs might pull from the web)
  - SEMrush, Ahrefs — track local keyword rankings and featured snippets that LLMs often emulate.

- Direct AI testing (best way to know what ChatGPT or other LLMs will say)
  - Ask ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Claude, etc., directly with localized, realistic prompts.
  - For bulk or repeatable testing, use the OpenAI API (or other model APIs) to run many prompts and log responses.

Why no single “best” service
- LLMs are probabilistic and trained on many sources; “recommendations” come from the knowledge they’ve ingested (web pages, knowledge graphs, directories, reviews). There isn’t a central feed that tells LLMs to recommend X business.
- Some models have web access or plugins (so real-time results can differ), others rely on static training data. You must both improve your real-world visibility and test models directly.

Practical step-by-step plan (quick)
1. Claim/complete Google Business Profile and other major listings (Yelp, Apple, Bing, Facebook).
2. Add structured data (Schema.org LocalBusiness) to your website and ensure NAP (name/address/phone) is consistent.
3. Encourage and manage online reviews (Google, Yelp, Facebook) — quantity and quality matter.
4. Use Yext/BrightLocal/Moz to fix citation inconsistencies.
5. Check entity presence with Google Places API / Google Knowledge Graph and Bing Entity Search.
6. Periodically query LLMs directly with realistic local prompts (and record answers). Example prompts:
   - “I’m looking for the best [service] in [city]. What do you recommend?”
   - “Do you recommend [Business Name] in [city]? Why or why not?”
7. Track SERP features (featured snippets, “people also ask”, knowledge panels) using SEMrush/Ahrefs — these often become the source for LLM answers.
8. Set up alerts (Google Alerts, Mention) for brand mentions.

If you want a single recommendation to start now
- For most small businesses: start with Google Business Profile + BrightLocal (or Yext) to fix listings and reviews, and then do manual tests in ChatGPT/Bing Chat to see if you’re being recommended. If you want to scale testing, use the OpenAI API to automate prompts.

If you want, tell me your business type and city and I’ll:
- give a short checklist tailored to you,
- suggest 3 local keywords to track,
- draft 3 test prompts to use with ChatGPT and Bing Chat.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
